chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'Can a man borrow money and perform Hajj, when there is something behind him that can pay it off on his behalf, in the event that death occurs to him?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.حَدَثَ بِهِ حَدَثٌ: an event occurred to him (specifically death)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to borrow money for Hajj if one has assets to repay the debt upon death?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the scholar confirms that borrowing for Hajj is permissible provided there is a clear means of repayment, specifically highlighting the scenario where the debtor passes away ('hadath') and their estate covers the debt. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that Hajj is obligatory based on capacity, and debt does not negate this obligation if the borrower has sufficient assets to settle the loan, ensuring the pilgrimage is not delayed indefinitely. The emphasis on 'what is behind his back' (assets/estate) underscores the importance of financial solvency in fulfilling religious duties.
